name: Hayabusa - Sigma-Based Windows Event Log Threat Hunting
description: Hayabusa is a fast Windows event log (EVTX) threat-hunting and forensics timeline generator. It applies a large built-in Sigma ruleset to .evtx files to flag attacker techniques - credential dumping, lateral movement, persistence, defense evasion - producing a prioritized, colorized timeline. A core blue-team tool for rapid triage of collected Windows logs.
notes:
=== GENERATE A DETECTION TIMELINE ===
  hayabusa.exe csv-timeline -d C:\evtx_logs -o timeline.csv
  # Single file:
  hayabusa.exe csv-timeline -f Security.evtx -o out.csv

=== LIVE ANALYSIS (local machine logs) ===
  hayabusa.exe csv-timeline -l -o live.csv

=== SUMMARY DASHBOARD ===
  hayabusa.exe metrics -d C:\evtx_logs       # event-ID frequency
  hayabusa.exe logon-summary -d C:\evtx_logs # logon stats (brute/spray)
  hayabusa.exe pivot-keywords-list -d C:\evtx_logs  # pivot indicators

=== TUNE SEVERITY / RULES ===
  hayabusa.exe csv-timeline -d logs -m high,critical   # only high+crit
  hayabusa.exe update-rules                             # refresh Sigma rules

=== JSON / OTHER OUTPUT ===
  hayabusa.exe json-timeline -d logs -o timeline.json

=== WORKFLOW (DFIR triage) ===
  # 1. Collect .evtx (KAPE / velociraptor / manual)
  # 2. hayabusa csv-timeline -> open in Timeline Explorer
  # 3. Filter critical/high, pivot on accounts + hosts + times
  # 4. Correlate with Sigma/YARA findings

=== ALTERNATIVES ===
  Chainsaw      # similar Sigma-over-EVTX hunting
  EvtxECmd      # EVTX to CSV (no detection logic)
  Sigma + SIEM  # rules applied in Splunk/Elastic/Sentinel

examples.label: Build detection timeline from EVTX dir

recommended.note: Hayabusa applies Sigma rules to EVTX.
Convert Sigma to other SIEM backends.
Pair with disk forensics in DFIR triage.

defense.why_it_works: Hayabusa is itself a defensive tool. It parses EVTX and matches Sigma detection logic to surface attacker behavior that is recorded in Windows event logs but easy to miss by hand.
defense.prerequisites: Collected .evtx files or live access to a Windows host; Hayabusa binary + rules.
defense.impact: Rapid identification of attacker activity (credential theft, lateral movement, persistence) during incident response.
defense.detection: This IS a detection tool - use it to detect. Ensure logging is configured so events exist to hunt: enable command-line auditing, PowerShell script-block logging, Sysmon.
defense.artifacts: N/A (defensive). Output timelines feed further investigation.
defense.splunk_spl: N/A - Hayabusa is an offline EVTX analysis tool; port its Sigma hits into Splunk for continuous detection
defense.sigma_rules: Uses the upstream Sigma ruleset (hayabusa-rules) against EVTX
defense.prevention: Maximize log fidelity (Sysmon, command-line + script-block auditing, sufficient log retention); centralize EVTX collection; run Hayabusa/Chainsaw as part of IR runbooks and periodic threat hunts.
